title: Embed-scale propagation and zero-copy dequant adapter for INT8/FP8 inference
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: When serving INT8/FP8 model variants we repeatedly pay dequantization costs and memory-copy overhead at layer boundaries and during KV prefill/restore. For streaming and bursty workloads the extra latency from per-request/hop dequant copies pushes tail latency above our 99th-percentile SLOs and increases GPU-to-host memory traffic, increasing cost.

Goal: Reduce per-request dequant overhead by propagating compact scale metadata (per-head/per-layer) through the KV/serialization path and performing dequantization only at the execution boundary with a zero-copy adapter. Combine this with a small mini-batch coalescing strategy at prefill time to amortize kernel launch cost while preserving latency SLOs. We expect to reduce dequant-associated latency by ~30-50% on common Llama-variant workloads and reduce memory traffic by up to 40% for prefill-dominated traces.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime has a configurable Embed-Scale header stored alongside serialized KV that preserves per-layer/per-head scale metadata without inflating KV size by >5%
New zero-copy dequant adapter integrates into attention kernels and avoids creating full float copies in GPU memory for standard prefill flows
99th-pct latency improvement of at least 25% on the internal qbench suite for int8 and fp8 variants compared to baseline release-1.20 for 0.5-2s prefill traces
Automated regression tests for correctness (numerical within tolerance) and deterministic fallbacks to safe dequant path when metadata is missing
Documentation and SDK flags exposing the feature: enable_embed_scale_propagation, zero_copy_dequant_mode
Canary rollout on <customer-dedicated> tier with telemetry and automatic rollback on error rates >0.5%
design_decision_log: 2026-02-22: Chose a per-head 16-bit scale + 8-bit exponent compact representation to balance precision and metadata size after experiments on Llama-2 13B (error < 1e-3 across quantized ops).
2026-02-25: Decided to keep metadata in KV blob header (prefill metadata zone) rather than embedding in each KV shard to simplify compatibility with offsite serialized snapshots.
2026-02-27: Opted for kernel-side lazy-dequant hook inside the fused attention epilogue rather than instrumenting all matmul kernels; simplifies interfacing with existing fused-attn implementations.
2026-03-03: Fall back to existing dequant+copy path when header checksum mismatch or metadata absent; log telemetrics and attach sample payload for debugging.
implementation_notes: Runtime changes: Add EmbedScale struct to KV metadata (C++ struct versioned). Add serialization/deserialization helpers for existing snapshot format.

Kernel changes: Add kernel entrypoint zero_copy_dequant_attn_epilogue that consumes quantized tensors and scale metadata directly from device-mapped memory and emits float outputs into ephemeral execution buffers without extra host<->device copies.

Scheduler: Implement mini-batch coalescer for prefill stage that groups short prefill requests (<= 16 tokens) arriving within a 1.5ms window, bounded by latency SLO percentiles. Coalescer has adaptive windowing inherited from existing batcher module.
Compatibility: Provide runtime flag to disable embed-scale propagation for older clients; on mismatch, route to regular dequant flow.
Telemetry: Instrument counters for metadata-missing rate, zero-copy success/failure, additional memory traffic delta, and per-request dequant latency.
perf_targets: Target: 25-50% reduction in per-request dequant latency (99th) for int8 and fp8 workloads (qbench scenarios: short-chat, code-complete, summarization).
Memory traffic: target 30-40% reduced GPU-host traffic for prefill-heavy traces on our staging traceset.
Compute overhead: kernel should not increase average per-token compute by more than 5% compared to fused-attn baseline.
test_plan: Unit tests: serialization round-trip for EmbedScale metadata, checksum and version compatibility tests.

Integration: End-to-end decode tests using quantized model artifacts (int8/fp8 mixed) ensuring output within numeric tolerance thresholds (L2 error < 1e-3 compared to float baseline for sample prompts).
Perf: Run qbench job 48h with and without feature flag across p99 and p50 metrics; compare memory bandwidth and kernel launch counts.
Canary: Deploy to 5% of hosted traffic and to a single Dedicated customer environment; validate telemetry and rollback automation.
Fuzzing: Feed malformed/older-format metadata and ensure deterministic fallback and no OOM/segfaults.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Metadata corruption could lead to incorrect dequant scale and degraded outputs. Mitigation: header checksum + versioning + strict fallback to safe copy-dequant path and alerting.
Risk: New kernel may regress some models numerically. Mitigation: run full eval-suite and require model-owners sign-off for enabling the flag on customer-dedicated deployments.
Risk: Coalescing increases latency for some singleton low-throughput requests. Mitigation: adaptive window based on percentile SLOs and opt-out flag per route.
